diagnosed: One real, reproducible mechanical breakage — unchanged, and its only correct fix lives entirely in a protected path: the research ESCALATION fast-lane is 100% broken. Scout/coverage-critic request a deep escalation via scripts/escalate-research.js -> `gh workflow run research-agent.yml -f tier=deep` using the job GITHUB_TOKEN, so the dispatched run's actor is github-actions[bot] (type: Bot). anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 now gates non-human actors and rejects bot actors unless listed in allowed_bots, which no step in research-agent.yml sets (the run config shows the default allowed_bots=""). Every escalated deep-research run therefore dies at its claude-code-action step with 'Action failed with error: Workflow initiated by non-human actor: github-actions (type: Bot). Add bot to allowed_bots list or use *'. Confirmed firsthand this run: workflow_dispatch run 42633516127 (2026-11-09T14:19Z, actor/triggering_actor both github-actions[bot]) failed BOTH the Fable 5 deep step and the Opus 4.8 deep-fallback step with that exact error; the escalation always passes -f tier=deep so only the two deep steps are exercised. Scheduled 4-hourly runs carry a human actor (CHaerem) so the gate is not consulted and they are unaffected — schedule runs Nov 10-12 are green; only the recall fast-lane is dead. The `gh workflow run` dispatch itself returns success, so escalate-research.js reports success, masking the failure (and closing any escalation-failed issue) except as red research runs. ALREADY TRACKED by OPEN issue #430 ('Research escalation fast-lane is 100% broken (bot actor rejected by claude-code-action)'), which carries the full format-resolved fix.
notes: Local health is clean: `npm test` green (1550 tests, 88 files); `node scripts/validate-events.js` reports 0 errors (59 events; warnings only — 5 landing-page-only channel URLs WP-246, 3 weak-time-basis advisories WP-242 — none are failures); docs/data/publish-freshness.json status=fresh (lag 0h, live==repo 2026-11-12T10:31:41Z); docs/data/usage-state.json green (week 62%, unifiedStatus=allowed, skipAll=false) — so the research failures are NOT quota skips.

OWNER FIX NEEDED (protected .github/workflows/research-agent.yml) — ALREADY TRACKED by OPEN issue #430: add `allowed_bots: "github-actions[bot]"` to the with: block of the claude-code-action@v1 step(s). Verified against the action source (src/github/validation/actor.ts isAllowedBot): both the configured value and the actor login are lowercased and have a trailing `[bot]` stripped before comparison, so `github-actions[bot]` and `github-actions` both match the github-actions[bot] actor equally. Do NOT use `*` on this public repo — the action's own action.yml warns an external App could then invoke it with a prompt it controls; scope to the one trusted first-party Actions bot, which is the only actor able to dispatch this workflow (requires actions:write). The escalation only ever dispatches -f tier=deep, so the two deep steps (Fable 5 'deep, preferred' and Opus 4.8 'deep fallback') are the load-bearing ones; adding it to the standard step too is harmless and keeps the three steps uniform. Safe because the research prompt is hardcoded in the workflow (not dispatcher-controlled), so this re-enables ONLY the recall fast-lane. Latest failed dispatch: 42633516127 (2026-11-09T14:19Z).

Could NOT author the fix: this is the unattended Self-repair CI agent (GITHUB_ACTIONS/CI context), so the CI-only scripts/hooks/protect-automation.js PreToolUse hook fires and BLOCKS any Edit/Write/Bash mutation of .github/workflows/** ('A human must author changes to these files'). Re-confirmed this run: on a self-repair/ branch the Edit adding allowed_bots to research-agent.yml was blocked by the hook (exit 2); branch deleted, working tree clean. By design (WP-139) an unattended CI agent cannot author protected-path (.github/workflows/**) changes — the hook is a hard safety invariant and was NOT circumvented (no API/indirect-write workaround attempted) — so no PR is possible and the fix must be applied by a human.

No non-protected fix exists: the breakage is the bot-actor gate on the dispatched run. Any GITHUB_TOKEN-authenticated `gh workflow run`/repository_dispatch produces a Bot actor regardless of event, so changing escalate-research.js cannot make the dispatch a human actor without a new PAT secret + workflow wiring (itself a protected change). The one-line allowed_bots addition is the correct, minimal fix.
